subject: economics
title: Monopsony and Trade Unions
welcome_lead: When power is unequal, classic supply-and-demand breaks down.
meta_desc: A-Level Labour Markets: monopsony, trade unions, wage setting.
final_note: Monopsony and unions can both move outcomes away from competitive equilibrium.

concepts.def: Negotiating pay and terms on behalf of members.
Party with power to set rather than take the wage.
Withdrawal of labour to press demands.
Monopsony employer faces a union - outcome depends on bargaining.

walkthroughs.body_html: A monopsonist faces an upward-sloping labour supply curve. Hiring one more worker raises the wage for all - so marginal cost of labour exceeds the wage. Result: lower wages and employment than competition.
Trade unions raise wages above competitive levels through collective bargaining. If labour demand is elastic, employment falls - but in monopsony, unions can raise both wages and employment.
When a monopsony meets a strong union, outcomes depend on relative bargaining power - strike funds, alternative options, public opinion all matter.

mcqs.q: In a competitive labour market, a union typically:
options: Lowers wages and raises employment
Raises wages and may reduce employment
Has no effect on wages
Eliminates strikes
Wages above competitive level
Wages below competitive level
Wages equal to MRP
Wages at zero

mcqs.q: What does standard theory predict about a minimum wage?
options: If above equilibrium, it raises wages for those still employed but causes unemployment by reducing labour demand — though empirical evidence is mixed.
A minimum wage is paid by the government.
Comparative advantage means richer countries should help poorer ones.
A minimum wage always reduces unemployment because workers have more money to spend.

mcqs.q: Is a trade deficit necessarily bad?
options: Not necessarily — it can reflect strong domestic demand, attractive investment opportunities, or borrowing to fund growth. Context matters more than the headline figure.
A trade deficit always means a country is losing wealth and failing economically.
A minimum wage is paid by the government.
A trade deficit means a country has no factories.

mcqs.q: What is the principle of comparative advantage?
options: A country should produce whatever it can make best.
Countries should specialise in producing goods with lower opportunity cost relative to others — even a country worse at everything still has a comparative advantage in something.
Comparative advantage means richer countries should help poorer ones.
A trade deficit means a country has no factories.
